summary: PARTIAL. Verified live in the VS Code integrated browser: entry adds is-visible and reaches opacity 1 (confirmed by screenshot); exit goes is-exiting -> animate-reset with opacity 0 and animation none; REPLAY fires fresh animationstart on both .about-section and .about-card, proving the entry animation genuinely restarts from the beginning rather than snapping to the end state; descendants covered for .about-card, .experience-list li, .section-header h2 and the dynamically injected #featured-projects cards; re-entry cleanly recovers from a mid-exit state (self-healing). Reduced motion: all four sections force-visible, opacity 1, animation none, full a11y tree renders. Other pages: zero console errors, grids populate (6/4/2 cards), replayAttrs 0. BLOCKED ON: real scroll gestures. The integrated browser will not scroll this document (scrollTo, html.scrollTop and mouse.wheel all no-op despite scrollHeight 3120 vs innerHeight 768), so scroll-driven entry/exit could not be exercised end to end. The code path was driven instead by shifting layout (documentElement.marginTop) and calling AnimationObserver.refresh(), which invokes the same evaluateReplaySections() the scroll handler uses. Also note rAF and CSS animation progression are throttled in this context until a paint is forced (screenshot), so computed opacity reads 0 until then. Needs confirmation by scrolling in a normal browser window.
